I verified the fix with a reproduction script and by running the existing tests.<channel|>The issue was that the `clear_meta_and_links` method in `rich/style.py` was copying the cached hash (`_hash`) from the original style object, even though the meta and link information—which are part of the hash calculation—were being removed. This caused the new style object to have an incorrect hash, identical to the original style's hash. I fixed this by setting `style._hash = None` in `clear_meta_and_links`, which forces the hash to be recalculated based on the updated (cleared) meta and link attributes. I verified the fix with a reproduction test case and by running the existing test suite.
